assessment.nobel_worthiness: Random-coefficients discrete-choice demand estimation with endogenous prices, together with the associated dynamic industry models, changed how demand, market power, mergers and welfare are measured. It is now standard in empirical IO, antitrust and trade, and its methodological and practical reach is very broad.
assessment.attribution: The core demand-side contribution is Berry (1994) and Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes (1995), with Pakes the leading figure through the dynamic framework (Ericson-Pakes) and the later estimation work. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin also made significant contributions, so the three-person limit forces a hard attribution choice. Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn are the most defensible trio for the demand-estimation core.
assessment.maturity: The central work dates from the 1990s and has been confirmed over decades by wide use in academia, regulators and industry. Timing is not a concern.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers to recognise the demand-estimation core or a broader empirical-IO and dynamic-industry prize that includes Bresnahan.
Exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss and others under the three-name limit.
My own field proximity (industrial organisation) may bias my assessment upward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models, in which selection into exporting drives reallocation and gains from trade, were a conceptual change in international trade after the Krugman new-trade-theory prize. They link micro firm data to aggregate welfare and underpin much applied trade policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the key paper. Helpman is credited for the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus FDI and for broader theory of trade with firm heterogeneity. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are not on this ballot's credited list, also made closely related contributions. Redding's work on quantitative extensions is more recent.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation in theory and in empirical work on firm-level data. The framework is well established.
uncertainties: Credit division with the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum empirical work, which is outside the credited names.
Helpman also appears on another ballot (political economy of protection), which may complicate how his work is credited.
My own field proximity (international trade and pricing) may bias my assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification and moment inequalities established a rigorous framework for inference under weak, credible assumptions. They reshaped how identification and the interpretation of evidence are understood, with applications from treatment effects to structural models and policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the clear originator (bounds, the identification problem, treatment-response analysis). Tamer is the leading contributor on moment inequalities and set identification in game and discrete-choice models. Molinari has made major contributions to inference but is the third name of three, so including her would require dropping no one but adds attribution breadth.
assessment.maturity: Manski's foundational work spans four decades. Moment-inequality inference has matured over the past twenty years. Recognition is long overdue relative to the importance of the ideas.
uncertainties: Whether the Committee sees this as sufficiently recognised after the 2021 prize for causal inference methods.
Credit allocation between Manski's foundational ideas and the later inference literature.
The practical influence of bounds approaches on applied empirical work is smaller than that of design-based methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation literature quantifies how distortions in the allocation of inputs across heterogeneous firms account for large cross-country income differences in TFP. This offered a micro-founded, measurable channel for development and growth and has been widely applied to policy questions.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the pivotal paper; Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) is its conceptual companion. The credited trio fits the origins of the literature. Restuccia has a strong claim on the theory, while Hsieh and Klenow have the dominant empirical effect.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of replication and extension across countries and sectors. The measurement approach is influential but has been debated.
uncertainties: Measurement sensitivity: markups, adjustment costs and measurement error can be mistaken for misallocation.
Rogerson, who is not credited, is the co-author of the key Restuccia paper.
Whether the contribution is viewed as a measurement framework or a fundamental discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The empirical optimal taxation programme links the elasticity of taxable income to optimal tax formulas, giving the Mirrlees tradition a sufficient-statistics, evidence-based form. It has had a strong influence on public finance and on tax policy debates.
assessment.attribution: Slemrod is the key figure on taxable-income responses and tax avoidance (behavioural responses, with Feldstein's 1995 contribution; Feldstein is deceased). Saez developed the sufficient-statistics formulas and the empirical evidence. Chetty's related contributions are better captured elsewhere, and Stantcheva's are more recent.
assessment.maturity: Twenty-five years of cumulative work. Some elasticity estimates remain contested, but the framework is firmly established.
uncertainties: Saez also appears in the top-incomes ballot, so his credit overlaps.
Feldstein's foundational role cannot be recognised because he is deceased.
Disagreement over the size of the elasticity of taxable income and the role of avoidance versus real responses.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Monopsony and imperfect competition in labour markets challenge the competitive benchmark for wage determination, with consequences for minimum wages, wage inequality and competition policy. It has strong conceptual and empirical grounding.
assessment.attribution: Manning's Monopsony in Motion is the main synthesis; Ashenfelter has long been associated with empirical labour-market design and wage-setting evidence. The extent to which monopsony as a separate discovery goes beyond the 2021 recognition of natural-experiment minimum-wage evidence is unclear. Naidu's work is more recent and is left out.
assessment.maturity: The theory is old, but the empirical revival and the broad policy influence are recent, so confirmation is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2021 Card prize and the minimum-wage literature may reduce its appeal as a separate discovery.
Magnitude of monopsony power remains debated in empirical work.
Exact attribution among many contributors, including Card, Krueger and Bhaskar, who are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Task-based accounts of technological change and the measured local labour-market effects of import competition changed the understanding of wage inequality, polarisation and the distributional costs of trade, which has strong policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Autor-Levy-Murnane's task framework and the China-shock papers (Autor-Dorn-Hanson) are the key contributions. The credited trio fits the China-shock work, while the task approach is closely tied to Autor and to Acemoglu, who has already received the prize.
assessment.maturity: About a decade for the China-shock research. Replication and re-examination are still ongoing, and some magnitudes are debated.
uncertainties: Debate about identification, persistence and magnitude of the China shock.
Overlap with Acemoglu's recognised work on technology and tasks.
Whether the maturity bar is met.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal open-economy framework (the Redux model and the Foundations of International Macroeconomics) provided the micro-founded workhorse for international macro, including nominal rigidity and welfare analysis of exchange-rate regimes. The exchange-rate disconnect puzzles identify a lasting empirical challenge.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are jointly the authors of the central framework. Rogoff's other work (for example, on exchange-rate puzzles and financial crises) is credited separately on another ballot. The puzzles are credited to a wider group of contributors, so recognition would centre on the framework.
assessment.maturity: The Redux model dates from 1995, and the framework has been confirmed through its role in the open-economy New Keynesian models used by central banks.
uncertainties: The puzzles remain unresolved, so the lasting-discovery claim rests on the framework rather than the empirical resolution.
Competing claims for open-economy macro, including Gali-Monacelli, Clarida and Corsetti.
My own work on exchange-rate pass-through is adjacent to this area, which may bias my assessment.
